Artefact: shipped CSS and markup Commentary: not the product

Floating surfaces in the browser report

Iteration 2 of the tooltip gallery. That page chose one tooltip; this one starts from a bug (the speaker picker cut off on the project dashboard) and audits every menu, picker, popover, tooltip and toast the theme draws: where it is placed, its shadow, its z-index. An investigation: nothing in the product changes with it. Generated from the tree by tooltip-gallery-v2.gen.py; rerun it after a theme change.

1. The person picker on the dashboard

Measured here…
Commentary

The picker is an absolutely positioned <ul> inside its badge's .bn-person-picker-anchor (SpeakerPickerTrigger.tsx). The pane it opens in, .bn-dashboard-pane, sets overflow-x: auto so a wide table scrolls sideways. CSS cannot scroll one axis and leave the other visible: when one axis is not visible, a visible on the other computes to auto. So the pane is a scroll box in both directions, and the part of the picker that hangs below the last row is inside it, behind a scrollbar. The probe line under each frame reads this from the engine you have this page open in.

The Mac app is fine because it never draws this <ul>: openNativePicker hands the same model to an AppKit popover, which is a window of its own.

Measured here…
Commentary

Proof of cause, not a fix. Taking the overflow away lets the picker float, but the pane is there to scroll a wide table sideways at narrow widths, and every other control inside it would now be one rule away from the same bug. overflow-x: clip would not help either: it keeps the other axis visible, but it cuts a wide table instead of scrolling it, and it still cuts a picker that hangs off the pane's right edge.

Measured here…
Commentary

The picker is the same element with the same classes, moved to the end of <body> and given position: fixed at its badge's bottom-left corner (this page's script, standing in for createPortal). No ancestor can cut it, because it has none but <body>. The app already does this for one floating surface: TapestryThumb.tsx portals the tapestry's hover frame and places it from a measured rect. Dialogs and toasts portal too.

Measured here: …. That decides whether the in-place shortcut (leave the picker where it is, make it position: fixed) is available: layout containment, which container-type can bring with it, makes the container the containing block for fixed children, and then they are cut like absolute ones. Even where it is not trapped, the shortcut is fragile: any ancestor that later gains a transform, filter or will-change (an animation, say) traps it again, and it needs the same measured placement a portal does. The portal costs the same and has nothing to go wrong under it.

2. Every floating surface

Commentary

22 surfaces. 15 are placed in flow: absolutely positioned inside the element that opens them, so each is exposed to the same bug wherever an ancestor scrolls, clips or contains paint. The house has already patched this three times, one host at a time:

  • bristlenose/theme/molecules/tag-input.css:103: raise the card with an open suggestion list over its siblings.
  • bristlenose/theme/molecules/tag-input.css:116: turn off the card's content-visibility (paint containment) while it is open.
  • frontend/src/islands/discussion/discussion.css:387: the same for a Discussion block.

Each patch fixes one host for one surface. The picker on the dashboard is the fourth host, and it cannot be patched the same way, because the pane's overflow has a job.

3. Every floating shadow, light and dark

Commentary

13 distinct shadows for what is, at most, four levels (raised, floating, notification, modal). 7 are written as fixed colours, so they ignore the palette and stay the same in dark, where a 4–12% black shadow on a near-black page draws nothing: compare the right-hand box of each pair. One writes its own dark value with light-dark(). Those built on --bn-colour-shadow (10% black in light, 40% in dark, tinted per palette) are the only ones that still show a faint edge in dark, and even there the 1px border is doing most of the work. The tooltip spec in theme/CLAUDE.md writes its shadow as a literal, so the written rule is itself one of the dark-mode misses. The tapestry popover borrows --bn-focus-shadow, a focus token, for elevation.

Commentary

5. Decisions this asks for

Commentary

Nothing here is built. The decisions, in the order they unblock the picker fix:

1Floating layer ruleAnything that floats over content (menu, dropdown, picker, popover, tooltip) renders in a floating layer at the end of <body>, never in flow. One shared primitive does the portal, the placement from the trigger's rect, flipping above when there is no room below, and repositioning on scroll and resize. The picker is the first user; the others move as they are touched. Owner call: one primitive now, or the picker alone first.
2Placement engineHand-rolled (as TapestryThumb does) or the platform's popover attribute and CSS anchor positioning, which put the surface in the top layer and need no portal. Browser and WKWebView support for anchor positioning has to be measured on the Mac targets before it is chosen; this page has not measured it.
3Elevation tokensTwo new shadow tokens, --bn-popover-shadow (every menu, picker, popover, tooltip, one value, as macOS draws menus and popovers alike) and --bn-notification-shadow (toast, chip), built only from colour tokens that exist, beside --bn-overlay-shadow and --bn-modal-shadow. --bn-control-raised-shadow is a control, not a floating surface, and stays. Decided 26 Nov 2026 (owner): B, the shadow plus the dialog's hairline in place of the border, and --bn-notification-shadow for toasts and the chip.
4z-index ladderTwo new layers, --bn-sticky-z and --bn-popover-z, beside --bn-overlay-z and --bn-toast-z. With a floating layer the per-component values (the 1, 2, 10 and 20 that lift one card over its sibling) stop being needed. Decided 26 Nov 2026 (owner): menus above dialogs, --bn-popover-z: 1050.
5Where the rule livesPromote the tooltip spec in bristlenose/theme/CLAUDE.md to a floating-surfaces spec (layer, shadow token, radius, border, motion), and replace its literal shadow with the token. That spec is the only written rule today and it covers tooltips alone.

6. Token values (decided 26 Nov 2026)

Commentary

Decided by the owner on 26 Nov 2026: B, menus above dialogs, and the notification token. Decisions 1, 2 and 5 are still open. The tokens are in a block headed DECIDED at the end of this page's theme CSS; nothing in the tree has them yet. Each frame below is the shipped picker on the dashboard pane's background, light on the left and dark on the right, with its shadow the only thing that changes. A is the two-layer geometry the tooltip spec already writes (0 4px 16px plus 0 1px 4px, the Screens menu's value), coloured by --bn-colour-shadow instead of fixed black, so it follows the palette and deepens to 40% in dark. B moves a second variable: it borrows the dialog's --bn-modal-hairline (10% black in light, 14% white in dark) as a ring in place of the 1px border, which is how the dialog already keeps its edge in dark, and how macOS draws a menu's edge on a dark desktop.

Commentary

What to look for: in light, A and B are close to today, a touch deeper. In dark, a black shadow on the near-black page barely registers whatever its strength, so the edge has to come from something lighter than the page: B's white hairline does that, A's border (#2d2d2d on #1c1c1c in the default palette) only faintly. B touches one more rule per surface (the border colour), so it is the larger change. Switch Palette to Edo to see both follow the warm shadow colour in light.

The ladder

  1. 1100--bn-toast-z (exists)toast, activity chip, AutoCode toast
  2. 1050--bn-popover-z (new)every menu, picker, popover, tooltip, drag ghost, in the floating layer
  3. 1000--bn-overlay-z (exists)dialog backdrop and dialog, contents overlay
  4. 100--bn-sticky-z (new)the toolbar (100 today), the transcript header (10) and the other sticky bars
  5. —Contentauto, or a local 1–2 inside one component; nothing floats here
Commentary

Menus above dialogs, below toasts. No menu opens inside a dialog today (the one candidate, TagInput in CodebookAuthoring.tsx, is outside its ConfirmDialogs), so this is a rule for the next one, not a fix. A floating surface opened from a dialog must draw over it, as a macOS popover over a sheet does; a page menu is closed by the click that opens a dialog, so putting the layer above the dialog costs nothing. A toast stays on top of everything, as --bn-toast-z already says. The 200, 300, 400 and the Screens menu's 1000 all become --bn-popover-z; the small local values that lift one card over its sibling go once their surface moves to the floating layer.
